claim: Dendritic cells (DCs) play an important role in anti-tumor immunity by inducing T cell differentiation.
source: Dendritic cells (DCs) play an important role in anti-tumor immunity by inducing T cell differentiation.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that is supported by established scientific knowledge about DC function in immunity.

claim: The DC mechanical sensor Piezo1 stimulated by mechanical stiffness or inflammatory signals directs the reciprocal differentiation of TH1 and regulatory T (Treg) cells in cancer.
source: Herein, we found that the DC mechanical sensor Piezo1 stimulated by mechanical stiffness or inflammatory signals directs the reciprocal differentiation of TH1 and regulatory T (Treg) cells in cancer.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study as stated in the abstract, supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Genetic deletion of Piezo1 in DCs inhibited the generation of TH1 cells while driving the development of Treg cells in promoting cancer growth in mice.
source: Genetic deletion of Piezo1 in DCs inhibited the generation of TH1 cells while driving the development of Treg cells in promoting cancer growth in mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from Piezo1 knockout mice shown in Figure 1 and related supplementary figures.

claim: Piezo1-deficient DCs regulated the secretion of the polarizing cytokines TGFβ1 and IL-12, leading to increased TGFβR2-p-Smad3 activity and decreased IL-12Rβ2-p-STAT4 activity while inducing the reciprocal differentiation of Treg and TH1 cells.
source: Mechanistically, Piezo1-deficient DCs regulated the secretion of the polarizing cytokines TGFβ1 and IL-12, leading to increased TGFβR2-p-Smad3 activity and decreased IL-12Rβ2-p-STAT4 activity while inducing the reciprocal differentiation of Treg and TH1 cells.
evidence: This mechanistic claim is supported by data shown in Figures 3 and 4 demonstrating cytokine production and signaling pathway activation.

claim: Piezo1 integrated the SIRT1-hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF1α)-dependent metabolic pathway and calcium-calcineurin-NFAT signaling pathway to orchestrate reciprocal TH1 and Treg lineage commitment through DC-derived IL-12 and TGFβ1.
source: In addition, Piezo1 integrated the SIRT1-hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF1α)-dependent metabolic pathway and calcium-calcineurin-NFAT signaling pathway to orchestrate reciprocal TH1 and Treg lineage commitment through DC-derived IL-12 and TGFβ1.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figures 5 and 6 showing the involvement of these signaling pathways.

claim: CD4+ T helper cells differentiate into different T cell subsets including TH1 cells, TH2 cells, TH9 cells, TH17 cells, and regulatory T (Treg) cells in specific cytokine environments.
source: CD4+ T helper cells play a central role in cancer by differentiating into different T cell subsets including TH1 cells, TH2 cells, TH9 cells, TH17 cells, and regulatory T (Treg) cells, in specific cytokine environments (Zhu et al., 2010; Adorini, 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature (Zhu et al., 2010; Adorini, 2003).

claim: Foreign antigens and innate stimuli are presented by antigen-presenting cells (APCs) to direct the development and differentiation of different subsets of CD4+ T cells in tumor.
source: Foreign antigens and all kinds of innate stimuli are often presented by antigen-presenting cells (APCs) to further direct the development and differentiation of different subsets of CD4+ T cells in tumor (Steinman et al., 2003; Marin et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature (Steinman et al., 2003; Marin et al., 2019).

claim: Inflammatory stimuli such as bacterial lipopolysaccharide (LPS), cytokine, or other innate stimuli such as oxygen, nutrient availability, and force and pressure can alter immune responses.
source: Inflammatory stimuli, such as bacterial lipopolysaccharide (LPS), cytokine, or other innate stimuli, such as oxygen, nutrient availability, and even force and pressure, can alter the immune responses.
evidence: This is a general statement about immune regulation supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: The tumor microenvironment integrates different innate physiological or pathological stimuli to develop a complex stimulation microenvironment.
source: In particular, the tumor microenvironment often integrates different innate physiological or pathological stimuli to develop a complex stimulation microenvironment (Solis et al., 2019; Geng et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature (Solis et al., 2019; Geng et al., 2021).

claim: Dendritic cells respond to various exogenous and endogenous stimuli through costimulatory molecule expression, T cell receptor (TCR) signaling, and cytokine production.
source: As professional APCs, dendritic cells (DCs) respond to various exogenous and endogenous stimuli mainly through three key signal pathways, including costimulatory molecule expression, T cell receptor (TCR) signaling, and cytokine production, bridging innate and adaptive immunity, and regulating the differentiation of different T cell subsets (Zhu et al., 2010; Murphy and Stockinger, 2010; Zhou et al., 2008; Chi, 2012; McKinstry et al., 2010; Li and Flavell, 2008; Stockinger et al., 2007; Zhu and Paul, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: DC-derived cytokines and chemokines exert proinflammatory or anti-inflammatory effects and are involved in shaping distinct T cell subset lineage programs to determine the prognosis of cancer patients.
source: DC-derived cytokines and chemokines exert proinflammatory or anti-inflammatory effects and are involved in the shaping of distinct T cell subset lineage programs to determine the prognosis of cancer patients.
evidence: This is a general statement about DC function supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: Piezo1 was originally identified as a mechanically activated non-selective cation ion channel with significant permeability to calcium ions.
source: Piezo1 was originally identified as a mechanically activated non-selective cation ion channel with significant permeability to calcium ions, is evolutionary conserved and is involved in the proliferation and development of various types of cells in the context of various types of mechanical or innate stimuli.
evidence: This is a statement about the known properties of Piezo1 supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: Innate inflammatory stimulation or mechanical changes such as changes in stiffness can activate Piezo1 and trigger an inflammatory response.
source: It has been reported that innate inflammatory stimulation or mechanical changes, such as changes in stiffness, can activate Piezo1 and trigger an inflammatory response (Geng et al., 2021; Yang et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature (Geng et al., 2021; Yang et al., 2008).

claim: Piezo1 exerts significant regulatory effects on many kinds of immune cell functions including macrophages, DCs, and T cells in inflammation and cancer.
source: Piezo1 exerts significant regulatory effects on many kinds of immune cell functions including macrophages, DCs, and T cells in inflammation and cancer (Solis et al., 2019; Geng et al., 2021; Aykut et al., 2020; Atcha et al., 2021; Chakraborty et al., 2021; Jairaman et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Environmental stiffness can alter the secretion of inflammatory factors by DCs and the mechanical force receptor Piezo1 may be involved in this regulation.
source: As reported (Chakraborty et al., 2021; Liu et al., 2018), environmental stiffness can alter the secretion of inflammatory factors by DCs and the mechanical force receptor Piezo1 may be involved in this regulation.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature (Chakraborty et al., 2021; Liu et al., 2018).

claim: Sorted splenic DCs cultured on a stiff hydrogel (E=50 kPa) or plastic plates exhibited significantly enhanced expression of the proinflammatory cytokine IL-12 and diminished expression of the anti-inflammatory cytokine TGFβ1 compared with DCs cultured on a pliant hydrogel (E=2 kPa).
source: Sorted splenic DCs cultured on a stiff hydrogel (E=50 kPa) or plastic plates exhibited significantly enhanced expression of the proinflammatory cytokine IL-12 and diminished expression of the anti-inflammatory cytokine TGFβ1 compared with DCs cultured on a pliant hydrogel (E=2 kPa; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Substrate stiffness regulates inflammatory cytokine secretion by DCs.
source: This suggests that substrate stiffness could regulate inflammatory cytokine secretion by DCs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data on cytokine expression under different stiffness conditions.

claim: The expression of the mechanical force receptor Piezo1 was significantly upregulated in 50 kPa-conditioned hydrogels compared with 2 kPa-conditioned hydrogels, similar to that in DCs stimulated with the inflammatory stimulus LPS.
source: Moreover, the expression of the mechanical force receptor Piezo1 was significantly upregulated in 50 kPa-conditioned hydrogels compared with 2 kPa-conditioned hydrogels, similar to that in DCs stimulated with the inflammatory stimulus LPS (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 50 kPa-conditioned hydrogels significantly caused more IL-12 and less TGFβ1 compared with 2 kPa, and mechanical force receptor Piezo1-deficient DC cells significantly rescued them to normal level.
source: Although 50 kPa-conditioned hydrogels significantly caused more IL-12 and less TGFβ1 compared with 2 kPa, mechanical force receptor Piezo1-deficient DC cells significant rescue them to normal level (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Mechanical force receptor Piezo1 mediates the inflammatory cytokine production induced by substrate stiffness in DCs.
source: These data suggested that mechanical force receptor Piezo1 mediated the inflammatory cytokine production induced by substrate stiffness in DCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that Piezo1 deficiency rescues cytokine production changes induced by stiffness.

claim: DC-specific Piezo1 conditional knockout (Piezo1-/-) mice were generated with Piezo1flox/flox and Cd11c-cre.
source: To investigate the regulatory effect of Piezo1 expressed by DCs on T cell function, we generated DC-specific Piezo1 conditional knockout (Piezo1-/-) mice with Piezo1flox/flox and Cd11c-cre.
evidence: This describes the experimental method used to generate the knockout mice.

claim: Piezo1-/- mice showed no obvious abnormalities after birth.
source: Piezo1-/- mice showed no obvious abnormalities after birth.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental mice.

claim: After 40 weeks of age, Piezo1-/- mice showed lower weight loss and less T cell activation in mesenteric lymph nodes (MLNs), Peyer's patches (PPs), intraepithelial lymphocytes (IELs), and lamina propria lymphocytes (LPLs) than WT mice.
source: However, after 40 weeks of age, these mice showed lower weight loss and less T cell activation in mesenteric lymph nodes (MLNs), Peyer's patches (PPs), intraepithelial lymphocytes (IELs), and lamina propria lymphocytes (LPLs) than WT mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Piezo1 deficiency in DCs results in fewer IFNγ+ TH1 cells and more Foxp3+ Treg cells but does not affect the numbers of TH2 or TH17 cells.
source: Importantly, Piezo1 deficiency in DCs results in fewer IFNγ+ TH1 cells and more Foxp3+ Treg cells but does not affect the numbers of TH2 or TH17 cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: DC-specific Piezo1 deficiency alters the differentiation of TH1 and Treg cells in aged mice.
source: Thus, we conclude that DC-specific Piezo1 deficiency alters the differentiation of TH1 and Treg cells in aged mice, which might be related to clinical manifestations.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on T cell differentiation in aged Piezo1-/- mice.

claim: The rate of tumor growth was significantly faster and greater in Piezo1-/- than in WT mice in MC38 mouse colon cancer.
source: The rate of tumor growth was signiﬁcantly faster and greater in Piezo1-/- than in WT mice (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Piezo1-/- mice had more Foxp3+ Treg cells, fewer IFNγ+ TH1 cells, and normal numbers of TH2, TH17, CD8+T cell, and IFNγ+CD8+T cells in tumor tissue compared with WT control.
source: Piezo1-/- mice had more Foxp3+ Treg cells, fewer IFNγ+ TH1 cells, and normal numbers of TH2, TH17, CD8+T cell, and IFNγ+CD8+T cells in tumor tissue compared with WT control (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 4A-B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 4A-B.

claim: Both Tbx21 and Ifng levels were downregulated rapidly, Foxp3 expression in T cells was upregulated gradually, and Il4, Il10, Il17a, and Gata3, Rorgt expressions did not change in Piezo1-/- mice during tumor progression.
source: Both Tbx21 and Ifng levels were downregulated rapidly, Foxp3 expression in T cells was upregulated gradually, and Il4, Il10, Il17a, and Gata3, Rorgt expressions did not change in Piezo1-/- mice (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 4C.

claim: Similar tumor growth and T cell differentiation were observed in B16.F10 melanoma tumor.
source: Similar tumor growth and T cell differentiation were also observed in B16.F10 melanoma tumor (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: DC-specific Piezo1 deficiency directs Treg and TH1 cell differentiation to promote tumor growth in the context of tumor microenvironment.
source: Thus, these data suggest that DC-specific Piezo1 deficiency probably directs Treg and TH1 cell differentiation to promote the tumor growth in the context of tumor microenvironment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on tumor growth and T cell differentiation in Piezo1-/- mice.

claim: There are more Foxp3+Treg cells and less IFNγ+TH1 cells, but similar TH2 and TH17 cells in Piezo1-/- compared with WT bearing-tumor mice in antigen-specific T cell responses.
source: However, there are more Foxp3+Treg cells and less IFNγ+TH1 cells, but similar TH2 and TH17 cells in Piezo1-/- compared with WT bearing-tumor mice (Figure 1D–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D-E from adoptive transfer experiments.

claim: Piezo1 in DCs regulates the TH1 and Treg differentiation in tumor microenvironment with the antigen-specific manner.
source: These data suggest that Piezo1 in DCs regulates the TH1 and Treg differentiation in tumor microenvironment with the antigen-specific manner.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the adoptive transfer experiments showing antigen-specific T cell responses.

claim: T cell proliferation was comparable between WT and Piezo1-/- mice in adoptive transfer experiments.
source: T cell proliferation was comparable between the WT and Piezo1-/- mice (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Recipient mice immunized with Piezo1-/- splenic DCs exhibited more Foxp3+CD4+ T cells and less IFNγ+CD4+ T cells.
source: However, the recipient mice immunized with Piezo1-/- splenic DCs exhibited more Foxp3+CD4+ T cells and less IFNγ+CD4+ T cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from adoptive transfer experiments.

claim: Both WT and Piezo1-/- mice showed similar levels of IL-4 and IL-17 expression among donor CD4+ T cells in adoptive transfer experiments.
source: Both the WT and Piezo1-/- mice showed similar levels of IL-4 and IL-17 expression among donor CD4+ T cells (Figure 2B–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B-C.

claim: Donor cells immunized with Piezo1-/- DCs exhibited more Foxp3+ cells, fewer IFNγ+ cells, and similar numbers of IL-4+TH2 cells and IL-17A+TH17 cells in antigen-specific responses.
source: Although WT and Piezo1-/- showed similar T cell proliferation (Figure 2D), donor cells immunized with Piezo1-/- DCs exhibited more Foxp3+ cells, fewer IFNγ+ cells, and similar numbers of IL-4+TH2 cells and IL-17A+TH17 cells (Figure 2E–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D-F.

claim: Donor T cells from mice immunized with Piezo1-/- DCs conditioned with 50 kPa, but not 2 kPa, hydrogels included more Foxp3+ Treg cells and less IFNγ+ TH1 cells.
source: Donor T cells from mice immunized with Piezo1-/- DCs conditioned with 50 kPa, but not 2 kPa, hydrogels included more Foxp3+ Treg cells and less IFNγ+ TH1 cells (Figure 2G–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G-H.

claim: The mechanical sensor Piezo1 in DCs stimulated by innate inflammatory or stiffness stimuli directs the reciprocal differentiation of TH1 and Treg cells.
source: Altogether, these data suggest that the mechanical sensor Piezo1 in DCs stimulated by innate inflammatory or stiffness stimuli directs the reciprocal differentiation of TH1 and Treg cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the adoptive transfer experiments with different stimulation conditions.

claim: Polyclonal T cells or antigen-specific OTII T cells cocultured with Piezo1-/- DCs induced more Foxp3+Treg cell and less IFNγ+ TH1 cell than WT control DCs.
source: Polyclonal T cells or antigen-specific OTII T cells cocultured with Piezo1-/- DCs in the absence or presence of antigen induced more Foxp3+Treg cell and less IFNγ+ TH1 cell, even with a variety of Piezo1-/- DCs including splenic CD11b+ DC or CD8α+ DCs, than WT control DCs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Tbx21 and Ifng expression was significantly downregulated and Foxp3 expression was significantly upregulated in T cells cocultured with Piezo1-/- DCs.
source: Moreover, Tbx21 and Ifng expression was significantly downregulated and Foxp3 expression was significantly upregulated in T cells cocultured with Piezo1-/- DCs.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from in vitro coculture experiments.

claim: Il4, Il10, Il17a and Gata3, Rorgt expressions were similar in T cells cocultured with Piezo1-/- DCs or WT DCs.
source: However, Il4, Il10, Il17a and Gata3, Rorgt expressions were similar in T cells cocultured with Piezo1-/- DCs or WT DCs (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Piezo1 deficiency in different kinds of DCs including CD11b+ DC and CD8α+ DC subsets regulates the reciprocal differentiation of TH1 and Treg cells in an antigen-specific manner.
source: These data suggest that Piezo1 deficiency in different kinds of DCs including CD11b+ DC and CD8α+ DC subsets regulates the reciprocal differentiation of TH1 and Treg cells in an antigen-specific manner.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the in vitro coculture experiments with different DC subsets.

claim: Coculture of antigen-specific OTII T cells with Piezo1∆DC splenic CD11b+ DCs conditioned by 2 or 50 kPa hydrogels in the presence of antigen induced a higher expression of Foxp3 and a lower expression of IFNγ.
source: Coculture of antigen-specific OTII T cells with Piezo1∆DC splenic CD11b+ DCs conditioned by 2 or 50 kPa hydrogels in the presence of antigen induced a higher expression of Foxp3 and a lower expression of IFNγ (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B-C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B-C.

claim: Piezo1 signals are required for reciprocal TH1 and Treg cell differentiation directed by DCs in an antigen-specific manner.
source: Together, Piezo1 signals are required for reciprocal TH1 and Treg cell differentiation directed by DCs in an antigen-specific manner.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the in vitro coculture experiments.

claim: Piezo1 deficiency does not alter the cell homeostasis level in DCs.
source: Piezo1 deficient does not alter the cell homeostasis level (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A), the expression of MHC, the costimulatory molecules CD80, CD86, CD54, PDL1, PDL2, and CCR7 expressions in DCs (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B-C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A-C.

claim: The phagocytosis activities of DC to IgG-coated beads is comparable between WT and Piezo1-/- DCs.
source: And, the phagocytosis activities of DC to IgG-coated beads is also comparable between WT and Piezo1-/- DCs (Figure 3—figure supplement 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3D.

claim: Piezo1-/- DCs have less IL-12 (p70) and more TGFβ1 expression in MLNs at 40 weeks of age.
source: First, we isolated the DC from MLNs at 40 weeks of age mice and found that Piezo1-/- DCs have less IL-12 (p70) and more TGFβ1 expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4A.

claim: The intestinal environment receives continuous antigen stimulation from microorganisms or food, which may lead to changes in intestinal tension and target the Piezo1 signal of DCs to trigger the differentiation of different subsets of T cells in aged mice.
source: These suggest the intestinal environment receives continuous antigen stimulation from microorganisms or food, which may lead to changes in intestinal tension caused by intestinal movements such as food digestion and absorption or inflammatory stimuli, and target the Piezo1 signal of DCs to trigger the differentiation of different subsets of T cells in the aged mice.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data on intestinal DC function in aged mice.

claim: Piezo1-/- caused DCs significantly higher TGFβ1 production and lower IL-12 (p40), IL-12 (p70), but not IL-23 production in the presence of LPS.
source: Next, we found that Piezo1-/- caused DCs significantly higher TGFβ1 production and lower IL-12 (p40), IL-12 (p70), but not IL-23 production in the presence of LPS (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 4B-C) or 50 kPa, but not 2 kPa, hydrogels (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A-B and Figure 3—figure supplement 4B-C.

claim: The polarizing cytokines TGFβ1 and IL-12 are involved in regulating T cell subset differentiation induced by Piezo1 in DCs stimulating by inflammatory stimuli or stiffness signals.
source: These results together suggest that the polarizing cytokines TGFβ1 and IL-12 are probably involved in regulating T cell subset differentiation induced by Piezo1 in DCs stimulating by inflammatory stimuli or stiffness signals.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cytokine production data.

claim: Adding IL-12 to the coculture system almost completely recovered the proportion of Piezo1-/- DCs during TH1 cell differentiation.
source: Although Piezo1 deficiency in DCs caused a significantly lower IFNγ+ TH1 cell percentage, adding IL-12 to the coculture system almost completely recovered the proportion of Piezo1-/- DCs during TH1 cell differentiation (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Blocking TGFβ1 signaling with an anti-TGFβ1 antibody in the coculture system almost completely recovered the effect of Piezo1-/- splenic DCs on Treg cell differentiation.
source: Consistently, blocking TGFβ1 signaling with an anti-TGFβ1 antibody in the coculture system almost completely recovered the effect of Piezo1-/- splenic DCs on Treg cell differentiation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from antibody blocking experiments.

claim: DC-specific Piezo1 expression regulates the reciprocal differentiation of TH1 and Treg cells through the polarizing cytokines IL-12 and TGFβ1.
source: Thus, we could conclude that DC-specific Piezo1 expression regulates the reciprocal differentiation of TH1 and Treg cells through the polarizing cytokines IL-12 and TGFβ1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cytokine supplementation and blocking experiments.

claim: Piezo1 deficiency in splenic DCs significantly increased the expression of TGFβR2 and decreased the expression of IL-12Rβ2 but did not affect the expression of TGFβR1/3 or IL-12Rβ1 on T cells in a DC-T coculture system.
source: Piezo1 deficiency in splenic DCs significantly increased the expression of TGFβR2 and decreased the expression of IL-12Rβ2 but did not affect the expression of TGFβR1/3 or IL-12Rβ1 on T cells in a DC-T coculture system (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Piezo1-deficient DCs exhibited significantly higher levels of phosphorylated Smad3 and lower levels of phosphorylated STAT4 than WT DCs.
source: Interestingly, Piezo1-deficient DCs also exhibited significantly higher levels of phosphorylated Smad3 and lower levels of phosphorylated STAT4 than WT DCs (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: TGFβR2-p-Smad3 or IL-12Rβ2-p-STAT4 signaling is involved in the Treg and TH1 cell differentiation induced by DC-specific Piezo1 expression.
source: These data suggest that TGFβR2-p-Smad3 or IL-12Rβ2-p-STAT4 signaling is involved in the Treg and TH1 cell differentiation induced by DC-specific Piezo1 expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the receptor expression and signaling data.

claim: Knockdown of TGFβR2 or IL-12Rβ2 expression significantly recovered the effects of DC-specific Piezo1 deficiency on T cell differentiation compared with the WT conditions.
source: Although DC-specific Piezo1 deficiency resulted in significantly more Foxp3+ Treg cells, higher phosphorylation of Smad3, and less IFNγ+ TH1 cells, lower phosphorylation of STAT4, knockdown of TGFβR2 or IL-12Rβ2 expression significantly recovered these effects compared with the WT conditions (Figure 4C–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C-D.

claim: TGFβR2-pSmda3 and IL-12Rβ2-pSTAT4 signaling in T cells are required for the T cell differentiation induced by DC Piezo1.
source: These data suggest that TGFβR2-pSmda3 and IL-12Rβ2-pSTAT4 signaling in T cells are required for the T cell differentiation induced by DC Piezo1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the receptor knockdown experiments.

claim: LPS treatment led to an increase in the proton production rate (PPR) in splenic DCs.
source: LPS treatment led to an increase in the proton production rate (PPR), but splenic DCs treated with the Piezo1 agonist Yoda1 exhibited significantly enhanced PPR values and expression of glycolytic molecules but not oxygen consumption rates (OCRs) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Splenic DCs treated with the Piezo1 agonist Yoda1 exhibited significantly enhanced PPR values and expression of glycolytic molecules but not oxygen consumption rates (OCRs).
source: LPS treatment led to an increase in the proton production rate (PPR), but splenic DCs treated with the Piezo1 agonist Yoda1 exhibited significantly enhanced PPR values and expression of glycolytic molecules but not oxygen consumption rates (OCRs) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Blocking glycolysis with 2-deoxy-D-glucose (2-DG) significantly recovered the IL-12 and TGFβ1 production in splenic DCs induced by Yoda1 treatment.
source: Blocking glycolysis with 2-deoxy-D-glucose (2-DG), a prototypical inhibitor of glycolysis pathways, significantly recovered the IL-12 and TGFβ1 production in splenic DCs induced by Yoda1 treatment (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Piezo1 deficiency in DCs significantly decreased the PPR value and the expression of glycolytic molecules but not the OCR value.
source: Furthermore, Piezo1 deficiency in DCs significantly decreased the PPR value and the expression of glycolytic molecules but not the OCR value (Figure 5A–C, Figure 5—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A-C and Figure 5—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Blocking glycolysis with 2-DG significantly recovered the productions of IL-12 and TGFβ1 in Piezo1-/- DCs to normal level compared with WT DCs.
source: Blocking glycolysis with 2-DG significantly recovered the productions of IL-12 and TGFβ1 in Piezo1-/- DCs to normal level compared with WT DCs (Figure 5A–C, Figure 5—figure supplement 3B-C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A-C and Figure 5—figure supplement 3B-C.

claim: Glycolysis activities are required for the polarizing cytokine production in DCs induced by Piezo1.
source: These data altogether suggest that glycolysis activities are required for the polarizing cytokine production in DCs induced by Piezo1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the glycolysis inhibition experiments.

claim: LPS activated all downstream pathways in WT DCs including p-JNK, p-Erk, p-p38, SIRT1, and HIF1α signal pathway.
source: Additionally, as expected, LPS activated all downstream pathways in WT DCs including p-JNK, p-Erk, p-p38, SIRT1, and HIF1α signal pathway.
evidence: This is an observation from the signaling pathway analysis.

claim: Piezo1 deletion in DCs enhanced the phosphorylation of Erk, p38, and JNK, similar to WT DCs.
source: However, Piezo1 deletion in DCs enhanced the phosphorylation of Erk, p38, and JNK, similar to WT DCs.
evidence: This is an observation from the signaling pathway analysis.

claim: Piezo1-/- DCs exhibited stronger and sustained activation of the histone deacetylase SIRT1 and weaker and shorter activation of the transcription factor HIF1α.
source: However, Piezo1-/- DCs exhibited stronger and sustained activation of the histone deacetylase SIRT1 and weaker and shorter activation of the transcription factor HIF1α (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Piezo1 is associated with SIRT1-HIF1α signaling and glycolysis activation.
source: Thus, Piezo1 is probably associated with SIRT1-HIF1α signaling and glycolysis activation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the signaling pathway analysis.

claim: Less IL-12 and more TGFβ1 production in Piezo1-/- DCs was significantly reversed in Piezo1-SIRT1 DKO cells.
source: Interestingly, less IL-12 and more TGFβ1 production in Piezo1-/- DCs was significantly reversed in Piezo1-SIRT1 DKO cells (Figure 5E, Figure 5—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 4A.

claim: HIF1α expression and glycolysis activities were significantly recovered to a normal level in Piezo1-SIRT1 DKO cells.
source: Consistently, HIF1α expression and glycolysis activities were significantly recovered to a normal level (Figure 5—figure supplement 4B-C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4B-C.

claim: SIRT1 is required for the IL-12 and TGFβ1 production in DCs induced by Piezo1 and HIF1α and glycolysis activation is related with these alterations.
source: These data suggest that SIRT1 is required for the IL-12 and TGFβ1 production in DCs induced by Piezo1 and HIF1α and glycolysis activation is probably related with these alterations.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the double knockout experiments.

claim: More IL-12 and less TGFβ1 in Yoda1-treated DCs was significantly reversed in Yoda1-treated Hif1a-/- DCs.
source: More IL-12 and less TGFβ1 in Yoda1-treated DCs was significantly reversed in Yoda1-treated Hif1a-/- DCs (Figure 5F, Figure 5—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 5A.

claim: HIF1α is required for the IL-12 and TGFβ1 production in DCs induced by Piezo1.
source: These data suggest that HIF1α is required for the IL-12 and TGFβ1 production in DCs induced by Piezo1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the HIF1α knockout experiments.

claim: SIRT1 expressions cannot be altered in Hif1a-/- DCs.
source: SIRT1 expressions cannot be altered in Hif1a-/- DCs (Figure 5—figure supplement 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5B.

claim: Treatment of Hif1a-/- with Yoda1 significantly reversed the alteration of glycolysis but not SIRT1 expression.
source: However, treatment of Hif1a-/- with Yoda1 significantly reversed the alteration of glycolysis but not SIRT1 expression (Figure 5—figure supplement 5B-C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5B-C.

claim: HIF1α and glycolysis is downstream targets of SIRT1 in regulating the Piezo1-induced cytokine production in DCs.
source: Thus, HIF1α and glycolysis is downstream targets of SIRT1 in regulating the Piezo1-induced cytokine production in DCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pathway analysis experiments.
